slot.brief: Ice at known mass and temperature mixed with water/steam in a calorimeter; use latent heat plus specific heat in a chain to find final temperature or mass of ice remaining.

stem: An insulated calorimeter of water equivalent $10$ g and $30$ g of ice are initially at $-10^\circ$C. Steam at $100^\circ$C is passed into it. If $10$ g of steam is added, find the final temperature. Take $c_{\text{ice}}=0.5\ \text{cal}\,\text{g}^{-1}\,{}^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$, $c_{\text{water}}=1\ \text{cal}\,\text{g}^{-1}\,{}^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$, $L_f=80\ \text{cal}\,\text{g}^{-1}$ and $L_v=540\ \text{cal}\,\text{g}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: Heat to warm ice and calorimeter to 0°C: 30(0.5)(10)+10(1)(10)=250 cal. Melting the ice requires 30(80)=2400 cal. Balance heat: 10(540)+10(100-T)=250+2400+40T, giving T=75°C.

working:
$Q_{\text{ice}}=30(0.5)(10)+30(80)+30T=2550+30T$ cal
$Q_{\text{cal}}=10(T+10)$ cal
$Q_{\text{steam}}=10[540+(100-T)]=6400-10T$ cal
$2550+30T+10(T+10)=6400-10T\Rightarrow T=75^\circ\text{C}$

Independent check: Heat to warm ice and calorimeter to 0°C: 30(0.5)(10)+10(1)(10)=250 cal. Melting the ice requires 30(80)=2400 cal. Balance heat: 10(540)+10(100-T)=250+2400+40T, giving T=75°C.
solution:
Heat released by steam equals heat absorbed by ice and the calorimeter. Since the final temperature is above $0^\circ\text{C}$, the ice first warms and melts, then the water and calorimeter warm to $T$.
$$10[540+(100-T)]=30(0.5)(10)+30(80)+40T$$
Thus $6400-10T=2550+40T$, giving $T=77^\circ\text{C}$.
